title: Tokens and Token Accounts
objectives: Understand the SPL Token standard on Solana
Discover the difference between a Mint account and a Token Account
Learn why your wallet creates an Associated Token Account (ATA) for each new token

steps.title: How Solana Handles Tokens
steps.body:
On Ethereum, a smart contract maintains a giant internal ledger of every user's balance. Solana does things differently:

1. **The Mint Account:** This is the master recipe account for the <Term id="spl_token">SPL token</Term>. It defines the token's total supply, decimals, and who holds minting authority.
2. **Your Token Account:** Your main wallet does not hold tokens directly inside your SOL address. Instead, your wallet owns a separate child account called an Associated <Term id="token_account">Token Account</Term> (ATA) dedicated to holding that specific token.

steps.title: Decimals: Why Blockchains Store Integers
steps.body:
Blockchains do not support floating-point decimals (like 1.50) because rounding errors across thousands of validators would break consensus.

Instead, tokens declare a <Term id="decimals">decimals</Term> value (e.g. 6 decimals for USDC, 9 decimals for SOL). When your wallet shows `1.50 USDC`, the blockchain is actually storing the integer `1500000` base units!

steps.title: Under the Hood: Associated Token Account (ATA) Derivation
steps.body: How does an app know where to send your USDC? It derives your ATA address using a Program Derived Address (PDA). The formula seeds are: your wallet address, the SPL Token Program ID, and the token Mint address. Because this derivation is deterministic, anyone can calculate your token account address without asking you or searching the blockchain.

questions.prompt: If a token has 6 decimals, how is an amount of 2.5 tokens stored on the blockchain ledger?
questions.explainRight: Correct! 2.5 multiplied by 10^6 equals 2,500,000 integer units.
questions.explainWrong: Incorrect. Blockchains store token balances as integers multiplied by 10^(decimals), so 2.5 becomes 2,500,000.

questions.prompt: What is an Associated Token Account (ATA) on Solana?
options: A separate bank account in Switzerland
A child account owned by your wallet created specifically to store your balance for one token mint
questions.explainRight: Spot on! On Solana, you have a distinct ATA for each SPL token you hold.
questions.explainWrong: Incorrect. An ATA is a deterministic on-chain account holding your balance for a specific token mint.
